I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the required wake-visual-signals skill to inspect the rollout evidence before touching the target policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted research shelf or neighboring configurations.

The skill requires the keyframe sheets to anchor the controller change. I’ve confirmed four sampled candidates, all successful; next I’m comparing the best finite run against the slower prefill and checking inherited notes for any informative failure mechanism before I write the required diagnosis.

The evidence favors one clear mechanism: bounded body-frame lateral counter-drift. Relative to the unchanged `0.25` bearing/rate anchor, its sampled `0.08` lookahead improved arrival by about 20.1 time units and mean distance by `0.141L`, doubled controller-relative upstream transport (`0.0160` vs `0.00793`), and reduced RMS lateral force, while the inherited sign-asymmetric rate gate missed the horizon. I’m recording that diagnosis before making the policy change, as the skill requires.

The diagnosis is now written. I’m implementing one candidate only: the best sampled counter-drift structure with a single bounded local change (`0.08 → 0.10` lookahead), while keeping propulsion, bearing/rate timing, posterior dynamics, and guards fixed. I’ll also add the durable lesson that the evidence supports `0.08` as the local anchor—without claiming the unevaluated `0.10` extension has already improved anything.

The reusable lesson now records the validated `0.08` mechanism, its effort tradeoff, and its falsification boundary. I’m invoking the mandated checker exactly as configured: guidance semantic check, lightweight Julia contract check, then the solver boundary check—no CFD rollout.

The first mandated check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent twice, so the checker cannot identify “exactly one” parent. I’m removing only the duplicated parent-list entry, preserving the assignment and all task content, then rerunning the check.

The guidance check passes. The Julia contract command is currently blocked by the environment (`julia: command not found`); the SSH messages are unrelated login-shell startup noise. I’m checking the configured runtime paths for an available Julia binary, then I’ll complete the boundary/schema checks independently if the runtime truly isn’t installed.

The boundary and deterministic parameter-schema checks pass; the candidate differs from the evaluated best policy only in the intended `0.08 → 0.10` constant plus comments. Since the workspace explicitly requires invoking its configured check-runner, I’m now handing that exact configuration an independent final verification; it may confirm the same missing-Julia environment limitation.
